summary: Partner learnings from the Red Carpet Copilot Program for building Business Central copilots: defining use cases is the hard first step, prompt engineering and continuous testing take the most time, and the work needs a focused team effort.
overview:
A partner describes what they learned in the Red Carpet Copilot Program, which helps partners turn concepts and ideas into AI-powered solutions their clients can use. The partner says getting started is the biggest challenge and that other partners also struggle with defining use cases.

The partner says the main effort in building a copilot function is prompt engineering, which takes time and needs continuous testing and validation to give customers the best answers. Automated testing is in place to check that copilot functions keep working as intended. The partner also says building a copilot should be a focused, team-based effort across the organization.
key_points: The Red Carpet Copilot Program helps partners turn concepts and ideas into AI-powered solutions for clients.
Getting started is the biggest challenge, and partners struggle with defining use cases.
The speaker says the difficulty is envisioning how to approach problems with AI, not the technical side.
Prompt engineering is time-consuming and was one of the biggest learnings.
Continuous testing is needed to find the best prompt so copilot gives the best answers to customers.
Automated tests are used to confirm copilot functions keep working as envisioned over time.
Build copilots as a team and make it a focused effort for the whole organization.
